title: Build a circuit breaker for a flaky vendor
prompt:
The reading app calls a text-to-speech (TTS) vendor. When the vendor is sick, every call hangs and fails, and your servers waste threads waiting. A circuit breaker notices the failures and starts failing fast for a while, so the app can show text without audio instead of falling over.

Implement class CircuitBreaker:

  • new CircuitBreaker({ failureThreshold, cooldownMs, clock }), where clock.now() returns milliseconds (injected, never Date.now()).
  • state: 'CLOSED' | 'OPEN' | 'HALF_OPEN'.
  • async call(fn): runs fn (an async function) according to the state, returns its result or rethrows its error unchanged.

Rules:

  • CLOSED: call through. A success resets the count. failureThreshold consecutive failures open the circuit.
  • OPEN: until cooldownMs has passed since opening, throw new CircuitOpenError() (provided; err.code === 'CIRCUIT_OPEN') without calling fn. Once it has passed, go HALF_OPEN.
  • HALF_OPEN: let exactly one trial call through. Success closes the circuit; failure re-opens it and restarts the cooldown. Calls arriving while the trial is in flight fail fast.
let t = 0; const clock = { now: () => t };
const cb = new CircuitBreaker({ failureThreshold: 3, cooldownMs: 5000, clock });
// 3 failures -> OPEN. At t = 4999 calls fail fast. At t = 5000 one trial goes through.

tests.name: closed: passes results and errors through unchanged
opens after 3 consecutive failures, then fails fast without calling fn
a success resets the consecutive-failure count
stays open for the cooldown, then a successful trial closes it
a failed trial re-opens the circuit and restarts the cooldown
half-open lets only one trial through at a time

hints: Handle the OPEN check first: if the cooldown has not passed, throw; if it has, set this.state = 'HALF_OPEN' and fall through. Track openedAt = this.clock.now() whenever you open.
For HALF_OPEN you need one extra field, e.g. this.trialInFlight. Set it to true before awaiting fn() (so a concurrent caller sees it), and reset it in a finally.

Shape:

if (this.state === 'HALF_OPEN') {
  if (this.trialInFlight) throw new CircuitOpenError();
  this.trialInFlight = true;
  try { const r = await fn(); this.state = 'CLOSED'; this.failures = 0; return r; }
  catch (e) { this.state = 'OPEN'; this.openedAt = this.clock.now(); throw e; }
  finally { this.trialInFlight = false; }
}
explain:
This is the pattern from Michael Nygard's Release It!, implemented in libraries like Resilience4j (Java), Polly (.NET) and opossum (Node), and built into service meshes like Envoy and Istio (as outlier detection and connection limits). Real breakers usually trip on a failure rate over a sliding window (for example 50% of the last 100 calls, with a minimum of 20 calls) instead of a simple consecutive count, and count slow calls as failures.

Say it in the interview: "Every call to a dependency gets a timeout, and the flaky or non-critical ones sit behind a circuit breaker. When it opens we fail fast and degrade (text without audio) instead of letting threads pile up waiting. Half-open lets one probe test recovery so we don't stampede the vendor the moment it comes back."
